title: The primitive-root cover after inverting its order
statement:
Let $N\ge1$ be an integer and let $C_N=\mathbf Z[1/N,T]/(\Phi_N(T))$, where $\Phi_N$ is the $N$th cyclotomic polynomial, characterized by the monic factorization $T^n-1=\prod_{d\mid n}\Phi_d(T)$ for positive $n$. Then
$$\operatorname{Spec}C_N\longrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/N]$$
is finite, etale and surjective [def-weil-affine-spectrum], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-etale-morphism]. If $\zeta$ is the class of $T$, then $\zeta^N=1$ and $1-\zeta^a$ is a unit of $C_N$ for every $1\le a<N$. In every algebraically closed geometric fibre, $\zeta$ is a primitive $N$th root of unity. Consequently, for every scheme $W$ on which $N$ is invertible, the projection $W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z[1/N]}\operatorname{Spec}C_N\to W$ is a finite surjective etale morphism; if a group acts on $W$ and trivially on $C_N$, the projection preserves the geometric inertia groups for that same group. Here a primitive $N$th root means an element of multiplicative order exactly $N$ (equivalently, its $N$th power is $1$ and no power with exponent $1\leq a<N$ is $1$). A geometric point is a morphism $\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to W$ for an algebraically closed field $\Omega$ [def-weil-geometric-point]; its geometric inertia is its stabilizer in the acting group. Fibre products are as in [def-pc-fibre-product], polynomial rings as in [def-weil-polynomial-ring], $\mathbf Z[1/N]$ as in [def-weil-ring-localization-away], and the quotient algebra as in [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient].

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.7, proof: the base change by Spec(Z[1/N,mu_N]), printed p.124. Primitive-root presentation of that base change.

proof.text: Put $R=\mathbf Z[1/N]$, $f=\Phi_{N,R}$ and $C=R[T]/(f)$. By [lem-per-cyclotomic-monic-positive-degree], $f$ is monic of positive degree $d$. By [lem-weil-pbc-monic-quotient-free], the classes of $1,T,\ldots,T^{d-1}$ form an $R$-basis of $C$, so $C$ is finite over $R$. The affine morphism $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is therefore finite by [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. In the defining cyclotomic factorization separate the factor indexed by $N$: $T^N-1=f(T)Q(T)$, with $Q=\prod_{e\mid N,\ e<N}\Phi_{e,R}$. Evaluating in the quotient gives $\zeta^N=1$, so $\zeta$ is a unit with inverse $\zeta^{N-1}$. For $N=1$ the product $Q$ is empty and equals $1$.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.7, p.124, primitive-root base change; finite-algebra verification by monic division

proof.text: Differentiate $T^N-1=fQ$ and evaluate at $\zeta$. Since $f(\zeta)=0$, this gives $N\zeta^{N-1}=f'(\zeta)Q(\zeta)$. Its left side is a unit: $N$ is inverted in $R$ and $\zeta$ is a unit by step 1. Thus $f'(\zeta)$ has inverse $Q(\zeta)(N\zeta^{N-1})^{-1}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-standard-etale-monic-derivative] with $S=R$ and $Q=f$. Its etale algebra $R[T,Y]/(f,Yf'-1)$ is isomorphic to $C$: send $T$ to $\zeta$ and $Y$ to this inverse; the inverse map sends the class of $T$ in $C$ to the class of $T$. The two composites fix $T$, and also $Y$ because an inverse of $f'$ is unique. Hence $\operatorname{Spec}C\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ is etale.

source.place: Tags 00UB, 00UC, definition-standard-etale and lemma-standard-etale (1), applied to the cyclotomic factorization

proof.text: For a prime $\mathfrak p\subset R$, take an algebraic closure $\Omega$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-algebraic-closure]. By coefficient naturality and positive degree in [lem-per-cyclotomic-monic-positive-degree], the image of $f$ in $\Omega[T]$ is the monic nonconstant polynomial $\Phi_{N,\Omega}$. Algebraic closedness gives a root $z\in\Omega$. Evaluation $R[T]\to\Omega$, $T\mapsto z$, kills $(f)$ and descends to $C\to\Omega$. Its kernel is a prime ideal whose contraction to $R$ is $\mathfrak p$: the coefficient map factors through the residue field and its injective field embedding in $\Omega$. The associated point of $\operatorname{Spec}C$ therefore maps to $\mathfrak p$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. Since every prime has such a lift, the morphism is surjective.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.7, p.124, surjectivity of the primitive-root base change; explicit geometric-point lifting

proof.text: For any field $K$ receiving an $R$-algebra homomorphism $C\to K$, let $z$ be the image of $\zeta$. The image of $N$ is invertible, hence nonzero. Coefficient naturality [lem-per-cyclotomic-monic-positive-degree] gives $\Phi_{N,K}(z)=0$, so [lem-per-cyclotomic-field-root-criterion] makes $z$ primitive of order $N$. In particular this applies to every $\Omega$-valued point of each geometric fibre, by composing it with the projection to $\operatorname{Spec}C$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-weil-geometric-point]. This proves the primitive-root assertion in every algebraically closed geometric fibre.

source.place: VIII Lemma 5.3.7, p.124, meaning of adjoining primitive roots; Mathlib cyclotomic root criterion

proof.text: Fix $1\leq a<N$. For every prime $\mathfrak q\subset C$, apply the field calculation in step 4 to $C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. If the residue of $1-\zeta^a$ were zero, primitivity would imply $N\mid a$, impossible for $0<a<N$. The kernel of $C\to\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is $\mathfrak q$: indeed $c/1\in\mathfrak qC_{\mathfrak q}$ exactly when $sc\in\mathfrak q$ for some $s\notin\mathfrak q$, and primality makes this equivalent to $c\in\mathfrak q$. Thus $1-\zeta^a$ belongs to no prime ideal. By clause (ii) of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-basic-opens-unit-ideal-quasi-compact] it is a unit. For $N=1$ there is no such $a$.

source.place: Tag 00E0, lemma-Zariski-topology, unit criterion; applied to the field-root calculation of step 4

proof.text: Let $W$ be any scheme on which $N$ is invertible. Its structural morphism factors uniquely through $\operatorname{Spec}R$: by [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], morphisms $W\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ correspond to ring maps $R\to\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$, and such a map exists and is unique because the integer $N$ is a unit of $\Gamma(W,\mathcal O_W)$ (it is one on every open), so $1/N$ must go to its inverse and $x/N^n\mapsto xN^{-n}$ is well defined [def-weil-ring-localization-away]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finite-morphism-permanence] clause (a), [lem-weil-pbc-etale-scheme-base-change], and [lem-weil-pbc-surjective-base-change] to the finite etale surjective morphism established in steps 1--3. Its base change $P=W\times_{\operatorname{Spec}R}\operatorname{Spec}C\to W$ is finite, etale and surjective. These three statements allow arbitrary schemes and arbitrary base changes, so no Noetherian, connectedness or reducedness assumption on $W$ is needed.

Let $G$ act on $W$ and trivially on $\operatorname{Spec}C$. Every automorphism $g$ of $W$ preserves its structural map to $\operatorname{Spec}R$: the composite with $g$ is again a morphism $W\to\operatorname{Spec}R$, hence equals the structural one by the uniqueness in step 6 [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-into-affine-scheme], so $G$ acts on $P$ by $g(w,c)=(gw,c)$. A geometric point $\bar y:\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to P$ is exactly a compatible pair $(\bar w,\bar c)$ of morphisms to the two factors [def-pc-fibre-product]. For each $g\in G$, the equality $g\bar y=\bar y$ holds if and only if $g\bar w=\bar w$ and $g\bar c=\bar c$, by uniqueness in the fibre-product universal property. The second equality always holds. Consequently $G_{\bar y}=G_{\bar w}$ as subgroups of the same $G$, and the inertia homomorphism of the projection is the identity on this subgroup.

source.place: VIII 5.3.6 and proof of Lemma 5.3.7, printed p.124, trivial action on the cyclotomic factor and inertness

split_report.summary: Expanded the primitive-root base change of ILO VIII 5.3.7 into seven steps. The derivative identity gives etaleness, positive-degree monic specialization gives surjectivity, the field-root criterion and prime-ideal unit test give unit differences, and the fibre-product universal property gives inertia equality. Added two exact Mathlib leaves for general polynomial facts, reusing all existing geometric tools. Statement hypotheses and conclusions are unchanged; primitive and inertia terminology is made explicit.

Steps 1--5 verify the cyclotomic ring; step 6 is its arbitrary base change; step 7 proves inertness for the same group.

lean.statement: theorem cyclotomic_finite_etale_cover (N : ℕ) (hN : 1 ≤ N) : IsFinite (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) ∧ Etale (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) ∧ Surjective (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) ∧ cyclotomicCoverRoot.{u} N ^ N = 1 ∧ (∀ a : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → a < N → IsUnit (1 - cyclotomicCoverRoot.{u} N ^ a)) ∧ (∀ (Ω : Type w) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (φ : cyclotomicCoverRing.{u} N →+* Ω), IsPrimitiveRoot (φ (cyclotomicCoverRoot.{u} N)) N) ∧ (∀ (W : Scheme.{u}), IsUnit (N : Scheme.Γ.obj (op W)) → ∃ s : W ⟶ Spec (.of (cyclotomicCoverBase.{u} N)), IsFinite (pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)) ∧ Etale (pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)) ∧ Surjective (pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)) ∧ ∀ (G : Type v) [Group G] (ρ : G →* Aut W), ∃! σ : G →* Aut (pullback s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)), (∀ g : G, (σ g).hom ≫ pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) = pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) ≫ (ρ g).hom ∧ (σ g).hom ≫ pullback.snd s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N) = pullback.snd s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)) ∧ ∀ (Ω : Type u) [Field Ω] [IsAlgClosed Ω] (y : Spec (.of Ω) ⟶ pullback s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)), {g : G | y ≫ (σ g).hom = y} = {g : G | (y ≫ pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)) ≫ (ρ g).hom = y ≫ pullback.fst s (cyclotomicCoverMap.{u} N)})
